penalties_applied.name: requires_physical_logistics
penalties_applied.reason: Any viable solution involves physical hardware (motion system, laser-cut jigs, tape reels) — fundamentally outside software-only delivery.

penalties_applied.name: requires_human_fulfillment
penalties_applied.reason: Even the software/SaaS portion (BOM-to-DXF generator) would require per-order calibration, hardware integration support, and physical kit fulfilment if hardware is included.

rationale: The pain is extremely vivid and real — solo hardware founders genuinely suffer through hand-soldering hours — but the solution is fundamentally a hardware + embedded-software product requiring physical manufacturing, shipping, and hands-on customer support. Claude and a simple web page cannot build or deliver a pick-and-place fixture or motion-system software. The buyer (solo hardware founders) is identifiable, but the niche is tiny and the build complexity is far beyond what this factory can produce autonomously. Operational autonomy scores 2 because every customer interaction involves physical hardware.
solution_plan: This is a semi-automated PCB assembly jig — part laser-cut hardware, part software to generate cutting templates from a BOM. It cannot be built or operated by a solo non-technical operator using Claude + a web form. Hardware design, sourcing, and physical fulfilment are required. A SaaS-only subset (BOM-to-DXF template generator) is technically buildable but has almost no standalone commercial value without the physical system. Drop this opportunity entirely.
notes: buildability_with_ai floor unmet (score 2, min 6). operational_autonomy floor unmet (score 2, min 7). Total 1.9 far below all thresholds.
